title: cmdpal: add support for multi-line input

proposed_comments.title: Apply the search preference in dock pages

confidence.rationale: Both SearchBar hosts were traced; ShellPage applies and updates the setting, while the dock host does neither.

proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The required initialization, settings-change subscription and disposal span unchanged DockPageControl files, so no single changed-line replacement is complete.
proposed_comments.body:
### Apply the search preference in dock pages

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Dock/DockPageControl.xaml` (`SearchBox`) and `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Dock/DockPageControl.xaml.cs` (constructor and `Dispose`); compare `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Pages/ShellPage.xaml.cs`.

**Problem:** With **Multi-line search input** turned off, a searchable page opened from the dock still uses the shared `SearchBar` wrapping defaults. `ShellPage` initializes and updates `SearchBox.MultilineSearchInput`, but `DockPageControl` does neither.

**Why it matters:** The dock search field wraps instead of scrolling horizontally even though the user disabled wrapping.

**Suggested change:**
1. When constructing the dock page, initialize its `SearchBox.MultilineSearchInput` from the saved setting, as the shell does.
2. While the dock page is open, propagate subsequent setting changes to the control on its UI dispatcher, and unregister any settings-change subscription when `DockPageControl` is disposed.

**Verification:** Disable the setting, open a searchable page from a dock item, and enter a long query; confirm it scrolls horizontally. Toggle the setting on and off while the page is open and confirm wrapping follows it. Close and reopen the page to verify the saved value is applied.
